steps: A client writes while both replicas initially hold v1.
The write reaches Replica A as communication to B fails.
The partition forces A to reject for consistency or accept for availability.
After healing, the system resumes one history or reconciles divergent versions.

lesson.scenario: A checkout preference is replicated across two regions when the inter-region link partitions.
entities: Accepts traffic in the west region
Accepts traffic in the east region

steps.title: Replicas agree
steps.narration: Both regions expose version 7 before the partition.
steps.outcome: The system starts consistent and available.
steps.invariant: CAP constrains behavior only when communication needed for an operation is partitioned.

steps.title: Link partitions
steps.narration: The inter-region path drops replication and acknowledgements.
steps.outcome: Each side can still receive local requests but cannot coordinate.
steps.invariant: A partition prevents simultaneously guaranteeing one history and success from both sides.

steps.title: CP choice rejects
steps.narration: West requires cross-region agreement and refuses the write.
steps.outcome: Consistency is preserved by sacrificing write availability.
steps.invariant: No acknowledged write may exist on only one side under the CP policy.

steps.title: AP choice accepts
steps.narration: With the policy switched to availability, west accepts a local version 8.
steps.outcome: Both sides remain available but expose divergent values.
steps.invariant: An AP response cannot promise linearizable cross-partition reads.

steps.title: Partition heals
steps.narration: Replication resumes and the conflict rule selects west version 8.
steps.outcome: The replicas converge after connectivity returns.
steps.invariant: CAP does not prescribe the reconciliation rule; the application must define it.
